subject: Incident wrap & remedial commitments — customer summary and RSVP
messages:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@habitat.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Incident wrap & remedial commitments — customer summary and RSVP

Hi Marta —

Thank you again for your patience while we completed our investigation. Attached is a customer-facing RCA and a machine-readable timeline (files attached to this thread). Below is a concise summary intended for your engineering and compliance teams, plus the concrete next steps we will take together.

High-level summary
- What happened: Between 09:03–09:18 PST we observed a sudden rise in per-request latency and a small fraction of 500s for your account. Root cause: an automated kernel rollout combined with an inadvertent cache eviction configuration rollback that caused increased KV-cache misses and CPU contention on the inference nodes serving your VPC.
- Impact: 11 minutes of elevated latency for ~3% of requests (affecting prefetched prompts and long-context queries). No customer data was exfiltrated; logs indicate only transient failures and successful retries.
- Root cause (short): rollout + config rollback -> cache thrash -> CPU throttling under the workload profile used by your account. Full technical details are in the attached RCA PDF.

Timeline (high level)
- 09:02 PST — automated kernel rollout started for a subset of nodes in us-west-2.
- 09:07 PST — we deployed a temporary config rollback to address unrelated kernel regressions (this rollback changed a cache eviction threshold).
- 09:10–09:18 PST — increased KV cache misses caused CPU run queue growth; retries produced elevated 5xx counts.
- 09:19 PST — mitigation: we reverted the rollback and isolated the affected pool; traffic migrated to healthy instances.
- 09:25 PST — metrics normalized.

Immediate customer-facing actions we are committing to (owners & ETA)
- Provide the full RCA document and a CSV timeline (attached) — Delivered (this email).
- Deploy a targeted patch to defend against config-rollback race conditions — Owner: Rohan Mehta (Eng) — ETA: 2026-11-25.
- Run a joint verification test with your infra team (simulate long-context load) — Owner: Priya Natarajan — Proposed window: 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-24.
- Add a durable guard and alert on eviction-threshold changes in your Dedicated pool — Owner: Olga Petrov — ETA: 2026-11-22.

Compensation & SLA next steps
- We propose one month service credit for impacted quota for November; if that is acceptable I will send the formal SLA credit note and process it through billing.

Attachments & links
- habitat_incident_rca.pdf (customer-friendly RCA)
- habitattimeline.csv (event-by-event machine timeline)
- service_snapshot.png (graph: p95 latency during event)
- Detailed engineering notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1aBcDEfGH-incident-rca
- HubSpot ticket: HS-82714

Request
- Please confirm availability for the verification run and whether the proposed credit amount works for you. If you’d like an alternate remediation cadence, tell us and we’ll adjust.

Apologies again for the disruption — we own this impact and will follow through on the items above.

Best,
Priya Natarajan
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
priya.n@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198

---
Attachments: habitat_incident_rca.pdf (PDF), habitattimeline.csv (CSV), service_snapshot.png (PNG)
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@habitat.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:40:12-08:00
Subject: Re: Incident wrap & remedial commitments — customer summary and RSVP

Thanks Priya — appreciate the quick turnaround and the clear timeline. A couple quick questions from our side: 

1) Can you confirm whether any user-request payloads were retried in a way that would create duplicate downstream writes? We run idempotent handlers but want to be sure.
2) About the credit — can you outline the proposed amount/percentage and how it will be applied to our invoices?
3) We’d like the joint verification run to include a slightly longer context (up to 32k) and a stress profile that mimics peak traffic on Mon/Tue mornings.

If we can get answers to 1–2 and lock a date for the verification run, we’ll route the postmortem to our compliance team.

—Marta
Marta Lopez
Head of Platform, Habitat.ai
marta.lopez@habitat.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T13:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Incident wrap & remedial commitments — customer summary and RSVP

Internal notes — do not forward raw: 
- On duplicates: engineering logs show retries were at the request layer and idempotency tokens were honored for Habitat requests; we did not see duplicate downstream writes. I’ll ask Rohan to include a short verification script that checks for duplicate processed IDs during the joint run.
- Compensation recommendation: offer one month credit for impacted capacity (equivalent to ~30% of Nov usage for the affected days). That gives a straightforward number for billing to process and is reasonable given impact and our SLAs.
- Verification test scope: include 32k context and a two-hour window that reproduces peak pattern (Mon 11/23 09:00–11:00 PST or Tue 11/24 09:00–11:00 PST). Rohan will own the test harness and runbook.

Marissa — I suggest we finalize the credit amount and send the customer the formal SLA credit note tomorrow morning. Olga, can you confirm the alert/guard ETA? Rohan — please confirm the patch plan ETA and whether you need a blue/green window.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Customer Success Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.n@redwood.ai>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@habitat.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Incident wrap & remedial commitments — customer summary and RSVP

Hi Marta —

Thanks for the quick reply and the requested clarifications. Short answers below and next steps.

1) Duplicate writes: confirmed — our logs indicate idempotency tokens were honored and we did not detect duplicate downstream writes for Habitat sessions during the window. We will include the verification script output in the joint test artifacts.

2) Credit: we are prepared to issue a one-month equivalent credit corresponding to the impacted quota (we estimate this as ~30% of your November bill attributable to the affected Dedicated pool hours). I will open the formal SLA credit note and route it to your billing contact today (HubSpot HS-82714). If you prefer a dollar amount instead of a percentage, we can convert and finalize in the credit note.

3) Verification run: we propose Mon 2026-11-23 09:00–11:00 PST. Rohan will execute the harness and share results in real time. Can you confirm the 32k context + peak profile? If that date/time works I will calendar invite the verification session and include runbook links.

4) Guard & patch ETA: Olga confirms she will deliver the alert/guard by 2026-11-22; Rohan confirms patch ETA 2026-11-25 (no mandatory blue/green required; we’ll stage to a small cohort first).

Next steps for today
- I will send the SLA credit note and billing workflow (expected by EOD PST).
- Tentatively schedule the verification window for Mon 11/23 09:00–11:00 PST; please confirm.
- Attachments above contain the full RCA and timeline; reach out if you need a deeper technical walkthrough prior to the verification run.

Again — we’re sorry for the disruption and appreciate your partnership.

Best,
Priya
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
priya.n@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0198
